ussd.subtitle: Dial our USSD shortcode on any mobile phone to access the same service — no internet, no data plan, no app required. The full prediction engine works on feature phones.

features.label: System capabilities
features.title: Built for the Malawian context
features.ai_desc: Trained on symptom patterns of Malawi-priority diseases using XGBoost, SVM, and Random Forest.
features.channels_desc: Smartphone users get a rich web interface. Feature phone users dial a shortcode.

faq.label: Frequently asked questions
faq.title: Answers to common questions
faq.q1: Is this a replacement for a doctor?
faq.a1: No. This system provides guidance based on reported symptoms. It does not diagnose. Always consult a qualified health worker for confirmation and treatment.
faq.q2: Do I need a smartphone to use it?
faq.a2: No. You can use the web version on any smartphone or computer, or dial our USSD shortcode on any mobile phone — including basic feature phones.
faq.a3: Yes. Your symptoms are processed securely and never shared with third parties. Creating an account is optional and only used to save your history.
faq.a4: The model is trained on symptom patterns of 11 Malawi-priority diseases, with strong recall across all conditions. However, it is a guidance tool, not a diagnostic device.
faq.a5: Malaria, typhoid, tuberculosis, dengue, five types of hepatitis, gastroenteritis, and pneumonia.
faq.a6: No. The web version is free. USSD may incur standard network charges from your mobile operator, which are typically minimal.

about.title: Health guidance, engineered for Malawi
about.intro: Malawi Health AI is an academic project that uses machine learning to help identify likely diseases based on reported symptoms, with prevention guidance tailored to Malawi's disease burden and language context.

mission.label: Our mission
mission.title: Bring early health guidance to every Malawian
mission.body: Most digital health tools assume a smartphone, an internet connection, and fluency in English. Our system was designed from the ground up to work for the people most likely to be left behind — feature-phone users, rural communities, and Chichewa speakers.

how.label: Technical architecture
how.title: How the system works
how.step1_desc: Users select from a curated list of symptoms via the web interface or the USSD menu. Inputs are validated and normalized before reaching the model.
how.step2_desc: Three models — XGBoost, Random Forest, and SVM — were trained on symptom-disease data filtered to 11 Malawi-priority conditions. XGBoost serves as the primary model in production.
how.step3_desc: A rule-based engine maps the predicted disease to actionable prevention and care advice, tailored to the Malawian context and available in both English and Chichewa.
how.step4_desc: Predictions reach users through a React web interface for smartphone owners and a USSD shortcode for feature phone users — same engine, same guidance.

disclaimer.title: Important notice
disclaimer.body: This system is not a substitute for professional medical care. Always consult a qualified health worker for diagnosis and treatment. If symptoms are severe or worsening, seek care immediately.
